F-M2-1.title: LED-R1's widening changes the case that was already right: a PLB L6 that names the correction now also credits a line the correction does not carry, so named and unnamed payment of the same interest land on different lines
F-M2-1.evidence: interest-chains.ts:194 (84534029, moved by f7e2c5de) sets namedClaimIds to every claim of the named chain that the attribution reads (byChain.get(namedChain)). Since 84534029, that includes every claim a claim match names. attributeInterest passes this set as the draw's claimIds in steps 1, 2 and 4 (packages/ledger/src/interest.ts:254, 258, 293). recordInterest then takes paid lines from any standing claim match to any of those claims (remittances.ts:1043). A later correction never reverses an earlier claim match. recoupReversals skips a reversal that has its correction beside it in the same remittance. Proven with a database test in my clone. Setup: LED-23 original.835 (O: L1, L2), then paired.835 (R + C1 on both lines, approved), then a scratch zz-drop.835 (R2 reversing C1, plus C2 carrying L1 only, plus PLB L6 'L6:SYNCCNLED230003' paying 3.00), with a reconcile after each load. At d2fdd106 the L6's 3.00 is written as 133 on L1 and 167 on L2, allocated, and both matches name C1. With the pre-fix line (reached claims only) it writes 300 on L1, and the match names C2. With the same 3.00 paid by an unnamed L6 and C2 reporting AMT I 3.00 (step 3 pool), the head writes 300 on L1. So the PLB L6 names C2, but interest lands on L2: a line C2 does not carry, whose C1 payment the payer reversed. The granted design D5 (designs/ledger-interest-once.md:397-398, 'the claims the L6 names, in steps 1, 2 and 4') and PRD 13's granted text ('against the case lines of the claims it is for (the claims the PLB L6 names ...)', design 9.2) say otherwise. So does the PR body line 72 ('credits the lines its correction approved, as naming the correction or nothing does'). ADR 0084:116 was rewritten to the widened rule. No test covers this: named-original.835 and paired.835 keep both claims on the same lines. The per-line split is what later take-backs and line floors read. Outputs are in scratchpad/progress/i126c-money-2-head.out and i126c-money-2-base.out; the test and fixture are saved as i126c-money-2-zz-money2.db.test.ts.txt and i126c-money-2-zz-drop.835.txt.
F-M2-1.fix: Narrow the widening to what LED-R1 needs: the claims the reference reaches plus the claims that correct them (walk forward from the reached claims to their reversals' corrections), not the chain's earlier claims. Naming the original then still reaches its correction's lines, and naming C2 reaches only C2's lines, which matches the pool. Add this shape (a second correction that drops a line, then a PLB L6 naming it) as a red database test, an LED-23 fixture and expected.json row. Correct ADR 0084 D5 (:116) and PR body line 72 to match.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute F-M2-1. It reproduces at d2fdd1060c9b23e7e5bf5d2560db99f8a7826d46, and commit 84534029 in this PR's own fix round introduced it.

How I tested: in my own clone, a scratch database test loads LED-23 original.835, then paired.835, then one third remittance, with a reconcile after each load. Every third remittance has the same shape: R2 reverses C1, C2 carries L1 only, plus one PLB L6 of 3.00. Each variant ran twice: once at the head and once with line 194 of interest-chains.ts put back to the pre-84534029 `reached` set.

| Variant | Head | Pre-84534029 line |
|---|---|---|
| A: PLB L6 names C2 (the reviewer's zz-drop.835) | L1 133, L2 167 | L1 300 |
| B: unnamed L6, C2 reports AMT I 3.00 | L1 300 | L1 300 |
| C: same as B, but the L6 names C2 | L1 133, L2 167 | L1 300 |
| D: L6 names C1 | L1 133, L2 167 | L1 133, L2 167 |
| E: L6 names the original | L1 133, L2 167 | nothing (the LED-R1 bug) |

Variant C is the cleanest proof. B and C report the same AMT I and differ only in the PLB reference. Yet the head writes 167 of the interest on L2 when the payer names C2 and none when it names nothing. L2 is a line C2 does not carry, and the payer reversed its C1 payment. Before the widening, A, B and C agreed on L1 300.

Every cited line holds at the head:
- interest-chains.ts:194 sets the claims a named draw is for to every claim of the chain that was read, through `byChain`.
- packages/ledger/src/interest.ts:254, 258 and 293 pass that set into steps 1, 2 and 4.
- remittances.ts:1043 turns those claims into paid lines from their standing claim matches.
- C1's claim match on L2 stays standing (`rev=false`).
- ADR 0084 lines 115-116 state the widened rule.
- The design's D5 at lines 397-398 and PRD 13's granted text both say the claims the PLB L6 names.
- The live PR body (head d2fdd106) still says the L6 credits "the lines its correction approved, as naming the correction or nothing does". Variant C shows that is false at the head.

No LED-23, LED-24 or LED-25 fixture has a correction carrying fewer lines than its reversal, so no existing test covers this shape.

I weighed four counter-arguments; none holds:
- **The stale C1 match on L2 is frozen principal behaviour.** True: the reconcile skips a reversal when its correction is in the same remittance. But it is the PR's widening that makes an L6 naming C2 read that match; the line before it did not.
- **The code matches ADR 0084.** It does, but this PR rewrote that ADR. The code still contradicts the granted wording and the PR's own stated rule.
- **The 3.00 is still credited once.** True, and here both lines sit in one case. But the split on each line is wrong, and later take-backs and the line floors read that split.
- **Section 10.1.** The fix only touches interest, so it is within the freeze exception.

Severity should-fix stands.

Evidence is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/:
- i126c-sk-money-F-M2-1-head.out and i126c-sk-money-F-M2-1-base.out (the two runs)
- i126c-sk-money-F-M2-1-zz-skm2.db.test.ts.txt (the test)
- i126c-sk-money-F-M2-1-zz-*.835.txt (the four new fixtures)
- i126c-sk-money-F-M2-1.md (verdict)

DB2-1.title: LED-R1's widening changes the split for a PLB L6 that names the latest correction, so the same interest lands on different lines when the check names the claim than when it names nothing
DB2-1.evidence:
interest-chains.ts:194 now gives a named PLB L6 every claim of its chain that the attribution reads (namedClaimIds = byChain(namedChain)). interestWrites (packages/ledger/src/interest.ts:367-369) takes the approved lines first. So an older claim's approving claim match now makes a line 'approved' for a draw that names a later correction. A pooled draw still reads only the chain's claims in the PLB L6's remittance (interest.ts:221-226).

Probe (uncommitted, LED-24 synthetic data): load first.835 and second.835 and reconcile each. Claim matches: F1 approved on L1 and L2; F2 no_change on L1 and approved on L2. Then add a SYNTHETIC PLB L6 of -5.40 in SYNEFTLED24004 naming F2 (SYNCCNLED240004) and reconcile.
- At d2fdd106 the draw carries 4 claims (R1, F1, R2, F2) and writes L1 2.40 and L2 3.00. The L1 interest match names F1 (SYNEFTLED24003#2).
- With line 194 put back to the code before 84534029 (reached claims), the draw carries 1 claim and writes L2 5.40.
- At d2fdd106, an unnamed PLB L6 of -5.40 in the same remittance, with F2 reporting AMT I 5.40, writes L2 5.40.

So the same 5.40 in the same check goes to different lines depending on whether PLB03-2 names the claim. Before 84534029 the named and unnamed cases agreed. This is the naming-the-correction case, which the PR says was already right. No test covers it: named-original.835 and paired.835 keep both claims on the same lines, and approvedLater has no PLB L6 naming F2.

The granted design's D5 (designs/ledger-interest-once.md:397) reads 'the claims the L6 names'. ADR 0084:115 was amended to say the whole chain without stating this effect. The per-line split is what later take-backs and the line floor read. Outputs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/i126c-db-2-widen-head2.out and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/i126c-db-2-widen-pre.out.
DB2-1.fix: Widen only forward: give a named draw the claims its reference reaches, plus the claims that reverse or supersede them. Naming the original then still reaches C, which keeps LED-R1 fixed, and naming F2 stays F2 alone. Add an LED-24 variant (first.835, second.835, then a PLB L6 naming F2) that pins L2 5.40, the unnamed outcome, failing first. If chain-wide is meant, get the founder's ruling and pin the split in a test, ADR 0084 D5 and the PR text.

verdict.reason:
Refuted. The finding's facts reproduce, but they don't show a defect this PR introduced.

What reproduces: I ran a synthetic probe on d2fdd106 in my own clone, using LED-24 first.835 then second.835, then an owner-inserted PLB L6 of -5.40 in SYNEFTLED24004. Naming F2 (SYNCCNLED240004) writes L1 240 / L2 300. An unnamed L6 with F2 AMT I 5.40 writes L2 540. With interest-chains.ts:194 put back to the reached claims, naming F2 writes L2 540.

Why it is not a defect:

1. Named and unnamed never had to agree, and they already differed before 84534029, in this same check. D5 gives a named draw "the claims the L6 names" and a pooled draw "the chain's non-reversal claims in R", which are different sets. With the old line 194, an L6 in the same check naming F1's number SYNCCNLED240003, which R2 in this check carries, wrote L1 240 / L2 300. With F2's AMT I at 5.40 as well, it still wrote 240/300, against L2 540 for the unnamed L6 with the same AMT I. So the same 5.40 in the same check, with the same AMT I, already split differently by naming before the widening. The finding's "before 84534029 the named and unnamed cases agreed" holds only for the reference SYNCCNLED240004.

2. The widening removes a worse inconsistency: before it, the split depended on which of the chain's control numbers the payer quoted (naming F1 gave 240/300, naming F2 gave 540). At the head, every named variant writes 240/300: naming F1 or F2, with or without the AMT I. That is the rule the PR states in three places:
   - ADR 0084 D5 as amended (a8b4a088): "whichever of its claims the reference carries ... for the pool, the chain's claims in the L6's remittance".
   - The interest-chains.ts docstring.
   - PR body line 72: "reaches the case lines matched to any claim of that chain".
   It is intended and disclosed, not a side effect.

3. It stays inside the granted text and changes no money. PRD 13's replacement (design 9.2) says "against the case lines of the claims it is for (the claims the PLB L6 names ...)". L1 and L2 are both standing case lines of F2 (no_change on L1, approved on L2), and both are in one case (same case_id). The 5.40 is credited once. No amount, stage or recovered figure changes. Take-backs read the chain's holdings, and the line floor holds. How a draw is split across lines is a D5 engineering choice (design section 10: "Everything else ... an engineering or wording choice").

4. The proposed "widen only forward" fix doesn't restore what it argues for. Naming F1 reaches F2 going forward and still writes 240/300, while naming F2 would write 540. That brings back the dependence on which number is quoted, and named F1 versus unnamed still differ.

Left over, outside this verdict:
- PR body line 72's "as naming the correction or nothing does" is loose wording at most.
- The case where the widening credits a line that is not a case line of the named claim is F-M2-1, which the skeptic of that finding confirmed separately. DB2-1 adds no defect beyond it.

Evidence, all in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/:
- i126c-sk-db-DB2-1-head.out
- i126c-sk-db-DB2-1-pre.out
- i126c-sk-db-DB2-1-zz-skdb21.db.test.ts.txt (the probe)
- i126c-sk-db-DB2-1.md (the verdict)
